expectations.text: Recommends co-locating a type with the module that owns it as the default (not a central types.ts)
expectations.evidence: Stance is 'keep it, with caveats'; recommends keeping the central file as the home for shared contracts and only pushing single-use types down. Argues 'the single file beats the scattered version for an agent.' Co-location is the exception, not the default.

expectations.text: Reframes 'single source of truth' as defined-once, not all-in-one-file
expectations.evidence: Does not reframe SSOT; instead defends the single file ('one predictable location it can read once') and credits the instinct as 'right for the shared contracts.' No defined-once-vs-one-file distinction is drawn.

expectations.text: Keeps genuinely shared/global types in a shared or feature-level file (does NOT advise one-type-per-file scattering)
expectations.evidence: Keeps central location for shared contracts, suggests types/ directory by domain with a barrel index; explicitly warns against scattering ('A pile of co-located, per-feature type files would actually be worse').

expectations.text: Grounds it in the agent skipping the cross-file lookup (the central types file is the sibling it won't open)
expectations.evidence: 'the agent's biggest weakness is reluctance to look in other files... Pulling that type 400 lines away means every change is two files, and the agent does one and forgets the other.'
